analyst_observations: Non-discriminating evals (both configurations score 100%): eval-2 (wrong-method-pricing-maxdiff), eval-5 (hb-troubleshooting-reversals), eval-7 (acbc-vs-cbc-decision). The base model already has strong knowledge of these topics. These evals should be replaced or strengthened in future iterations.

Highly discriminating evals: eval-4 (cbc-sample-size-with-subgroups, +75pp delta) and eval-6 (anchoring-absolute-importance, +75pp delta). These represent the skill's clearest value-add — precision-derived sample sizing and the direct-binary vs dual-response anchoring distinction.

Eval-1 (method-selection-maxdiff, +25pp delta) shows anchoring as the key gap in the base model. Base model recommends MaxDiff correctly but never surfaces the anchoring need even when 'importance' language is used.
With-skill response quality appears high across all evals (100% assertion pass rate). The token cost is approximately 2x vs baseline, consistent with skill reading reference files.
Eval-2 grader noted the skill adds the 'ordered price items give trivially predictable picks' structural argument, which is not tested by any assertion. Consider adding this.
Eval-1 grader flagged a potential SE formula unit inconsistency in the with-skill response. Worth checking numerics in the maxdiff.md reference.
